newsitem.title: THAILAND: RESEARCH ALERT - Supalai has cash flow worries.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT - Supalai has cash flow worries.

text.p: Thai property developer Supalai Plc faces negative cash flow in 1997 of around 107 million baht ($4.1 million) and is rated as an underperforming stock, Thaimex Finance and Securities said issued on Wednesday.

"The company may only book 28 million baht in interest but we estimate that in 1997 actual interest will come to around 660 million baht including interest on the 380 milliom in debentures outstanding. As a result free cash flows will be in the red by about 107 billion baht," it said in a report on the firm.
Supalai's 380 million baht debentures mature in September, and the current portion of long term loans which must be paid back this year, is another 891 million baht, Thaimex said.

"It appears the company is facing a dangerous period ahead - booked net profit should rise about nine percent in 1997, but only if everything goes according to plan will the firm be able (just) to meet its obligations," the report said.

"To right the situation the company is hoping to launch a new debenture for one billion baht - if this were successful and the long term debt due this year were rolled the outlook would be good, unfortunately success of the bond, even if scaled down is a big if," it added.
Thaimex said said the quality of Supalai's developments, rising revenues and profits would normally lead it to recommend the stock.
"However the precarious nature of the company's financing together with the growing reluctance of banks to lend to the sector means this stock is very risky," the report said. ($1 = 26 baht)
